items.title: Sanmina beats quarterly expectations and guides to strong FY2027 EMS and AI-infrastructure growth
items.summary: Sanmina reported fiscal Q4 revenue of $3.86 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.43, beating published estimates. Management forecasts $17.5–19.5 billion in FY2027 revenue after integrating ZT Systems. Early after-hours reports described a roughly 20% share-price jump; the move is not a confirmed close. Acquisition effects and leverage warrant scrutiny.

items.title: Hims & Hers reports 49% revenue growth but profit and margin deterioration
items.summary: Hims & Hers reported Q3 revenue of $890.4 million, up 49%, but gross margin fell to 57% from 74% and it posted a $33 million net loss. Management reduced adjusted EBITDA guidance and narrowed revenue expectations. Shares lost about 11.8% in regular trading and reportedly slipped further after hours. The margins and subscriber growth challenge the growth premium.

items.title: U.S. rebound holds into close as AMD and chipmakers rally while Nvidia declines
items.summary: The S&P 500 closed up 2.35% and Nasdaq 2.74%, confirming the earlier broad-market recovery. AMD gained about 13%, Broadcom roughly 9%, while Nvidia closed down 4.27% at $178.67 amid its board inquiry. The striking dispersion supports company-specific risk differentiation rather than an across-the-board AI demand collapse.

items.title: Brent settles down 5.85% at 10-week low despite continuing Hormuz vessel risk
items.summary: Brent settled November 9 at $92.57, down 5.85%, and WTI at $86.85, down 4.38%, extending the earlier intraday retreat. U.S. comments lowered expectations of renewed Iran strikes even as maritime attacks remain a risk. Physical Dated Brent weakness suggests reduced near-term tightness; no newly verified normal transit or additional production interruption was established.

items.title: Ionis drops nearly 28% as Tryngolza forecast halving hits commercialization outlook
items.summary: Ionis fell 27.83% to $28.45 at 10:35 AM EST, versus roughly 10% lower in earlier premarket reports. The company reduced Tryngolza 2026 product revenue guidance to about $50 million from $100–110 million, while reaffirming consolidated revenue guidance. The product shortfall is material; durability of prescriptions and reimbursement remain uncertain.
